chunks.text: More Pressure: common causes include blocked or restricted outlet, closed discharge valve with machine running, excess heat input, thermal expansion of blocked-in liquid, failure of pressure control.
No Flow: common causes include pump or compressor trip, suction valve closed, line blockage, upstream supply loss, control valve fails closed.
Less Flow: partial blockage, fouling, filter plugging, valve partially closed, machine running below capacity, pump cavitation at low NPSH, leakage to atmosphere.

Reverse Flow: occurs when downstream pressure exceeds upstream on machine trip or standby line-up; typical safeguard is a check valve at the discharge; consider backflow of process gas into utility headers.
More Temperature: loss of cooling medium, fouled cooler, fire case, machine recycle overheating, ambient extremes.
Less Pressure: excessive demand, supply failure, leak or rupture, vacuum created by condensation or draining with vents closed.
More Level: inlet exceeds outlet, level control failure, drain blocked; risk of liquid carryover into gas lines and machines.
No/Less Level: loss of inflow (upstream tank empty, drain or bypass valve passing), outlet stuck open; risk of pump dry running and gas blow-by to the downstream system.
